scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-01.statement: Of disputed bills split by read type, 1240 have read_type ESTIMATED and 1785 have read_type ACTUAL (billing-db).

F-03.statement: crm-tickets dispute_response_times shows median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, across 2440 tickets.

F-04.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records: no tariff changes logged.

F-05.statement: route-log route_completion_aug_sep shows completion rate 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual_read_accounts for period 2026-08..09.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 states route priority changes requested by the utility are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-AUTOMATION-FIXES-SU.statement: Dispute volume doubled mainly because ticket handling is slow/manual, and an AI auto-answer agent that also auto-corrects wrong bills will bring disputes back to baseline.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (logged in DA-RULES) around August caused reads to be mis-processed, producing incorrect bills and the dispute surge.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The nightly AMI export (H-MDMS-BILL) from the vendor-run MDMS started failing or delivering incomplete reads since August, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter reads (H-FIELD-BILL) became incomplete or erroneous since August, per the contracted field service, feeding wrong reads into billing.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-ERROR.statement: The 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step itself is systematically producing wrong bills (e.g., bad defaults or rising estimate frequency), independent of which upstream source is failing.

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db shows disputed bills split by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL — a majority of disputed bills involve ACTUAL (not estimate-substituted) reads, so upstream read-acquisition failure or estimate-substitution errors alone cannot explain most of the dispute surge; something is also wrong with bills built from accepted ACTUAL reads.

Monthly ticket counts show a step change from ~600/month in June-July 2026 (610, 590) to ~1180-1260/month in August-September 2026, confirming the roughly 2x surge magnitude and its August onset, but the counts alone do not indicate which upstream cause (billing, AMI, field reads, or response handling) is responsible.

crm-tickets dispute_response_times shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets — response handling is not breaching SLA, which weakens the premise that slow/manual response handling is driving the dispute surge.
billing-db.tariff_change_log returned zero records, indicating no tariff changes were logged — this rules out tariff changes as a contributing cause of the wrong bills / dispute surge.

Field route completion for manual meter reads was 0.88 against a 0.95 target during the Aug-Sep 2026 window, affecting 9200 manual-read accounts, indicating a shortfall in completed manual reads concurrent with the dispute surge.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that there has been no tariff change this year is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that agrees with the already-established authoritative finding (E-04, billing-db tariff_change_log) ruling out tariff changes as a cause.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortage of three meter readers since July causes routes to run late, so affected customers receive estimated bills; this is an unverified stakeholder attribution consistent with the authoritative route-completion shortfall (E-05) but does not itself confirm staffing as the cause, and comes from a stakeholder with a noted incentive to justify headcount increase.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) establishes that the utility may request route priority changes but they are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) — this is an authorization document, not causal evidence about the dispute surge, and it reaffirms the already-modeled K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement for push_route_update.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) enumerates 14 specific routes with individual completion rates (sample route R-00 at 0.7), giving route-level detail behind the aggregate manual-read completion shortfall (E-05); it identifies which routes are lagging but does not itself correlate these routes with disputed or estimate-substituted billing accounts.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) lists 320 accounts that received estimate-substituted bills last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes. This is the account-level dataset needed to join against E-09's 14 lagging routes per work item W-WI-CORRELATE-ROUTE-DISPUTES, but that join has not yet been executed, so it does not yet establish whether estimate-substituted billing concentrates on the lagging routes (still required to resolve VOB-R-2/U-FIELD-CAUSE-CORRELATION).
